rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 20 Sep 2028 (682 days left). This counts 2 years from 20 Sep 2026 (the date they refused; if they refused earlier, your deadline is earlier). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 340,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

support.text: You paid Rs 3,40,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law states District Commission has consideration up to Rs 50 lakh. Rs 3,40,000 is within this range, so the complaint goes to District Commission. The law text does not mention filing fees, so the claim of 'no filing fee' is not supported by this law text.

support.text: You paid Rs 3,40,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law states fee is Rs 200 for consideration above Rs 5 lakh up to 10 lakh. Rs 3,40,000 falls in this range, so there is a filing fee of Rs 200, not 'no filing fee'.

support.text: The showroom refusing to take back the defective bike and refund the money is an unfair trade practice.
support.reason: The law text explicitly lists 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid' as an unfair trade practice.

support.text: The bike being defective is a defect in goods under the law.
support.reason: The law defines 'defect' as 'any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard' and 'defective' is construed accordingly. A defective bike falls under this definition.

support.text: You can file the complaint in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in.
support.reason: The law text mentions filing with District Commission and electronic filing, but does not specify e-jagriti.gov.in as the online platform. The specific website URL is not in the law text.

support.reason: The law text states complaints must be filed within two years (730 days, not 682 days) from the date the cause of action arose, with possible condonation of delay for sufficient cause. The specific number 682 days and the warning 'Do not wait until the deadline' are not in the law text.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: Kanpur showroom, [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 01 September 2026 I paid Rs 340,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests, including on 20 September 2026, you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 340,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
